passage:
At the lunch table in a Manchester secondary school, Kayla leaned in with her phone. “You'll never guess what I heard about Tomasz. His dad lost his job and they're moving.” Three others leaned closer. Esther put down her fork. “I didn't hear that,” she said. “Did anyone finish the maths homework?” Kayla rolled her eyes. Someone muttered, “Boring.” Esther kept her face steady and asked again.

Siddiq, who had said nothing, glanced at her. The next week at the bus stop he said quietly, “Can I tell you something? I haven't told anyone.” Esther nodded. “I won't repeat it.” The others invited her less that month, but Siddiq sat next to her at lunch every day after that.

qa.q: What did Esther say when Kayla offered the rumour?
qa.a: Esther said, “I didn't hear that,” and asked whether anyone had finished the maths homework.

qa.q: What does Siddiq's glance at Esther suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Siddiq noticed Esther refuse to pass the rumour on and began to wonder whether Esther could be trusted with something private.

qa.q: What choice did Esther make when Siddiq asked to tell something?
qa.a: Esther nodded and promised not to repeat it.

qa.q: What might Tomasz feel if the table's talk about a dad's job reached Tomasz?
qa.a: Tomasz would probably feel exposed and embarrassed, and would value Esther's refusal to pass it on.

grounding: A teenager says they did not hear a rumour and changes the subject, losing a little popularity but becoming safe to confide in.

passage:
Evening study hour had ended and the hostel common room filled up. Dilnaz dragged a chair beside Nandini. “Listen, Meher was crying in the stairwell yesterday. Someone says her marks slipped and her parents are furious. Want to hear the rest?”

Nandini kept her eyes on her notebook. “I didn't hear that,” she said. “Did you finish the chemistry sheet?” Dilnaz waited for more, shrugged and turned to another girl, who was already leaning in.

Kavya, from the next bed, glanced up and gave Nandini a small smile. Later that night Kavya knocked on the door. “Can I ask you something and you won't tell anyone?” Nandini closed the door and sat down.

qa.q: Where was Meher crying, according to Dilnaz?
qa.a: Dilnaz said Meher was crying in the stairwell yesterday.

qa.q: Why did Nandini ask about the chemistry sheet?
qa.a: Nandini felt uncomfortable with the gossip about Meher and wanted to change the subject rather than pass the rumour on.

qa.q: What did Nandini do when Kavya knocked that night?
qa.a: Nandini closed the door and sat down to listen.

qa.q: What might Meher feel if the rumour spread through the hostel?
qa.a: Meher would probably feel exposed and ashamed, knowing private tears and worries were being discussed by others.

grounding: A teenager says they did not hear a rumour and changes the subject, at a small cost in popularity, and becomes someone safe to confide in.

passage:
Dear Lavanya,
You've moved to Pune and missed all the drama, so here's the update.
Remember Rhea? Someone started saying she was caught shoplifting at the mall. On Wednesday Ritesh tried to tell me the whole story at lunch. I just said, “I didn't hear that, and I don't want to,” and asked him about the cricket trials.
He rolled his eyes and told the others instead. For a week, that table was a little cold to me. I missed being in on things, honestly.
But yesterday Rhea herself came to me and told me her real worry, about her parents fighting. She said, “You're the only one who didn't pass that story around.”
So. Less popular, more trusted. I'll take it.
Saurabh

qa.q: What did Saurabh say when Ritesh tried to tell the story?
qa.a: Saurabh said, "I didn't hear that, and I don't want to."

qa.q: How did Saurabh feel during the cold week?
qa.a: Saurabh felt a little lonely, missing being in on things, but steady about the choice.

qa.q: What did Saurabh gain by refusing to pass on the rumour?
qa.a: Saurabh became someone safe to confide in, and Rhea trusted Saurabh with her real worry.

qa.q: How might Rhea have felt about the shoplifting rumour?
qa.a: She was probably hurt and ashamed, knowing people were passing around a story about her.

grounding: A teenager writes about refusing to pass on a rumour, losing a little popularity but becoming someone safe to confide in.

passage:
You want to know how I became the “safe friend”? I'm Joseph, and it started with one lunch break.
Siddharth sat next to me, grinning. “You won't believe what I heard about Nisha and the chemistry teacher.”
I didn't want to hear it. I just said, “Nah, I didn't hear that. Hey, did you finish the physics sheet?”
He stared at me. “You're so boring, man.” He went off to tell the others. For about two weeks I wasn't invited to their group call. It stung.
Then, slowly, people started telling me things. Real things. Aman told me about his brother's accident. Nisha herself told me the story was made up and thanked me.
Being boring turned out to be kind of useful.

qa.q: What did Siddharth call Joseph?
qa.a: He called Joseph "so boring".

qa.q: How did Joseph feel about not being invited to the group call?
qa.a: Joseph felt stung and a bit left out for about two weeks.

qa.q: Why did refusing the rumour pay off for Joseph?
qa.a: It showed Joseph could be trusted, so people later shared real, private things.

qa.q: How might Nisha have felt when she thanked Joseph?
qa.a: Nisha probably felt grateful and relieved that someone refused to spread a false story about her.

grounding: A teenager describes refusing a rumour by saying "I didn't hear that", which costs some popularity but builds trust.

passage:
I sit next to Kamal in Class 11, so I saw this happen, though I can only guess what he was thinking.
At break, Shankar came over with his phone. “Have you seen what they're saying about Neha? About why she left the hostel?” He was already scrolling to show us.
Kamal didn't look at the phone. He said, calmly, “Not interested, yaar,” and started talking about the football trials.
Shankar laughed. “Saint Kamal.” A couple of guys joined in the joke. Kamal just shrugged.
For a few days, Shankar's group left him out of stuff. But I noticed that the next week, when Neha came back to school, she sat next to Kamal at lunch. She didn't sit with anyone else.

qa.q: What did Kamal say to Shankar?
qa.a: He said, "Not interested, yaar."

qa.q: How did Kamal seem to feel when the guys joked about him?
qa.a: He seemed calm and unbothered, just shrugging rather than getting upset.

qa.q: What did Kamal's refusal achieve?
qa.a: It stopped the rumour with him and, though he lost a little status, it made him someone Neha felt safe with.

qa.q: How might Neha have felt coming back to school?
qa.a: She was likely nervous and wary, choosing to sit next to someone who hadn't spread the story.

grounding: A classmate describes a teenager calmly refusing a rumour, losing a little popularity but becoming someone safe to confide in.

passage:
Monday: On the school bus, Nirmala leaned over. "Did you hear why Tara's parents came to school? Apparently..." Rashmi said, "I didn't hear, and I don't really want to. Did you finish the physics sheet?" Nirmala rolled her eyes. "Boring." Two girls behind them giggled.
Thursday: At lunch the story about Tara was everywhere, and Rashmi was left out of a whispered huddle. "She won't gossip anyway," someone said. Rashmi ate her lemon rice by herself.
Two weeks later, Saturday: Tara messaged Rashmi. "Can I talk to you? You're the only one who didn't pass that stuff around." They met on the library steps, and Tara talked for an hour. Walking home, Rashmi thought the lonely lunch had been worth it.

qa.q: What did Rashmi ask Nirmala instead of hearing the story?
qa.a: "Did you finish the physics sheet?"

qa.q: How did Rashmi feel eating lunch by herself on Thursday?
qa.a: Rashmi felt lonely and a bit left out, paying a small price for not joining the gossip.

qa.q: What made Rashmi's way of refusing work?
qa.a: She didn't lecture; she just said she didn't want to hear and changed the subject, so there was nothing to argue with.

qa.q: Why might Tara have chosen Rashmi to talk to?
qa.a: Tara trusted Rashmi as the one person who hadn't spread the story, so Rashmi felt safe 🙂

grounding: Shows a teenager declining to hear a rumour and changing the subject, losing a little popularity but becoming someone safe to confide in.
